D013-D009_h001.question:
It’s been about five months now. I wake up already feeling like I’m under water. Everything I do is in slow motion—getting dressed, walking around the lot, even picking up keys feels like my body’s moving through mud. I used to be sharp, on my feet with customers; now I just stand there, staring, and my coworkers joke that I’m in “slow mode.”

I find myself tearing up over nothing—sitting in my office, in the car, even with a customer if they say something vaguely kind. I can’t hold it back. At night, my brain just loops every deal I messed up, every mistake in my marriage, things from years ago. I replay them over and over, telling myself I ruined everything.

Sometimes when I’m driving on the highway or standing on the top level of the parking structure, I get these urges to just veer into traffic or jump. I haven’t made any plans, but the impulses are there and they scare me.

There are days I feel a bit more energetic or talkative, like I’m “on,” but it never lasts more than a few hours, and I’ve never had one of those long “high” periods people describe. It’s just this same heavy low, day after day, and it’s wrecking my work and whatever life I have left outside the dealership.
D013-D009_h001.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D009_h002.question:
It’s been about five months now where I just feel…stuck in this heavy fog. I cry all the time, sometimes at my desk, sometimes in the bathroom at work, and it’s over stuff that doesn’t even seem that big. A client email, a minor typo in a press release, and I’m suddenly tearing up and can’t pull myself together.

I can’t sit still either. I’m constantly bouncing my leg in meetings or pacing around my apartment, picking at the skin on my fingers until they’re raw. It’s like my body is restless but my mind is exhausted.

I keep replaying little mistakes in my head and telling myself I’ve ruined my career already, that I’m a burden to my team and my friends. Even when people say it’s fine, I feel like I should be punished for messing up, like I don’t deserve this internship.

Most nights I lie in bed thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow. I’m not planning anything, but the idea of just…not existing feels like a relief.

Sometimes I get brief bursts where I feel a bit more energetic or chatty, but they never last more than a day, and I’ve never had those long, super-high phases people describe—nothing that ever felt like the opposite of this, just short blips that fade right back into the low. All of this is making it really hard to keep up at work and even with basic stuff like laundry or seeing friends.
D013-D009_h002.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D009_h003.question:

I don’t really feel sad so much as nothing. When I’m off air, I pace around my apartment, pick at my cuticles, scroll endlessly—I can’t sit still, but I’m not actually getting anything done.

I’ve started thinking I’m a fraud, that what I do doesn’t matter and that I don’t matter. Ratings are fine, my boss says I’m doing well, but I can’t shake this sense that I’m useless, that anyone could replace me and no one would notice. At night I’ll lie there thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I’m not planning anything, but the idea of being gone feels like a relief.

Sometimes I’ll have brief bursts where I talk faster, get a bunch of ideas for segments, stay up late planning, but they fizzle out within a day or two. I’ve never had a stretch where I felt wired or unusually “up” for days on end, nothing like that in my past—just these short spurts that quickly collapse back into this empty, agitated fog. It’s gotten to the point where even getting ready for the evening broadcast feels overwhelming.
D013-D009_h003.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D009_h004.question:

D013-D009_h005.question:

I think about dying every day—not in a detailed, planned way, more like wishing I just wouldn’t wake up, or that something would happen so I don’t have to keep doing this. Work has really slipped; I avoid clients, I can’t make decisions I used to make in minutes.

There are brief moments where I get a little more energy and start three or four new ideas for the company, stay up late reorganizing my apartment, but it never lasts more than a day or two and I don’t feel especially high or out of control—just restless. I’ve never had a period where I was clearly “up” for days, needing hardly any sleep and feeling on top of the world. It’s mostly this same, dragging low mood that just won’t let up.

A. Bipolar II Disorder

    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D009_h006.question:

Sometimes when I’m on a high floor at work or crossing a busy street, I get this sudden urge to just step off or walk into traffic. It’s like a pull. I haven’t planned anything, but it scares me.

Once in a while I’ll have a random burst where I talk more or feel a bit restless, but it fades fast. I’ve never had a period where I was wired for days, super happy or confident, or needed hardly any sleep.

Lately I’ve been thinking a lot about not being here. Not just vague thoughts—more like picturing specific ways and places I could do it. I haven’t done anything, but I’ve gone far enough in planning that it scares me.

Sometimes I’ll get brief spells where I feel a bit more energized or talkative than usual, but they’re short, not extreme, and I’ve never had a period where I was up for days or acting wildly out of character.

I don’t have a detailed plan, but the thoughts come strong, and it’s getting harder to just brush them off. It’s affecting my work and my marriage a lot.

I’ve been feeling like this for about a year, maybe a bit over—like 15 months. I cry all the time now, over the smallest things. Sometimes I’ll just be brushing out a dog and suddenly I’m tearing up for no real reason, and I have to turn away so the client doesn’t see.

Nights are the worst. I’ll get into bed around 11, but my mind just spins and I lie there for hours, staring at my phone or the ceiling. It takes forever to actually fall asleep, and then I’m exhausted at work the next day and moving in slow motion.

It’s gotten hard to do basic stuff. I’ll stand in front of my closet in the morning and literally can’t pick what to wear. Even choosing what to eat at lunch can take me so long that my break is almost over. My boss has noticed I’m slower and making more mistakes.

Sometimes when I’m crossing the street or on a bridge, I get these sudden urges to just step out into traffic or jump. I don’t have a plan, but the thought hits me hard and scares me.

There are days I feel a little more energetic or talkative, but it never lasts more than a day or so, and it’s nowhere near what people describe as those “high” phases—no wild spending, no staying up all night feeling amazing, nothing like that.
